Mains, a young man of twenty, running his first race for us, did very well over what is, perhaps, the most difficult stage of the lot, involving, as it does, the gradual ascent of the South Downs, culminating in the climb of Dale Hill.
Webb, Robertshaw and Mains. The furlong junior championship was a tragedy.

The “Bels” made a good start and with Mains early in the lead, closely followed by Carter, things looked quite rosy. At the end of the first circuit, three-quarters of a mile, we must have had all our 12 in the first 50 places.
The only two absentees were Penny and Mains, both of whom were suffering from leg injuries. Arthur Allum took the lead from the start and Jack Flower never got on terms with him again.
Saunders, Shields, Taylor, and our Erith friends, Mains and Shaw, all showed up well and will be strong challengers for premier places in our teams and worthy representatives of the Club.
Beverley Brook was passed and the Kingsmere reached, and here one of our men, Cecil Mains, went to the front, but appeared to be doubtful of the course.
With such a crowd of good boys as we have, anything may happen. Mains and Shaw tell me they are both keen on making a good show. This sounds encouraging with the "South of Thames" race in view.
Mains was on Carter's shoulder, then came our "second Footer"—Harry Shields—nearly a minute behind Penny! Cook, Rice, Shaw and Walker were in a string after this.

With Carter, Shields, Shaw, Mains, Rice, Mitchell (A.F.), Walker, Fletcher and others our team looks good. Also the "Sir Jeremiah Colman" Cup for the first team to finish 12 men (which we hold) must be retained.

Our two Kent members, Mains and Shaw, are proving their worth, and greatly assisted the team to gain second position to the Surrey A.C., our old rivals, whom we all congratulate on their splendid victory.
Doing a "traditional short-circle' 'round the golf-links, the runners had to cross the road, and at this point it was gratifying to see Footer, Penny, Allum, Mains and Flower all with the leaders.
Then came Allum, 48th, followed at close intervals by Mains, Shaw and Flower, whom I could not place, but who were all well inside in the 100 positions.
On the first circuit Mains forced the pace but on leaving the Common Allum led Carter by 30 yards, with Mains and Shields next some distance behind.

Our representatives to score were: Footer 1, Penny 3, Carter 17, Flower 25, Allum 37, Mains 40. All of which brings us to this year's race, when our objective was achieved and our first win recorded; but before proceeding with the pleasant task of describing our success, I should like to make a few comments.
